Subject: Tenant dependency matrix + slice inspector for console

Hi team,

Quick ask: ACME (Suresh is copied below) is asking for a single view that helps them understand per-tenant economics and operational risk when a route spikes. Right now they open multiple dashboard pages and ping us. The rough product ask is: a Console experience that shows, per-tenant and per-route, (1) token cost breakdown (model variant, quantization profile), (2) 95/99 latency percentiles with tail bucket, (3) cache hit / prefix-KV summary, and (4) a dependency matrix showing upstream services and model variants that contributed to the call (so they can see which model fallback or regional routing kicked in).

Desired behaviors:
- One-click drill: click tenant -> shows top 5 costly routes, sortable by cost or tail latency.
- Exportable CSV with tokens by model variant and hour (sample attached: example_export.csv).
- Fast dependency visualization (graph) for last 24h spikes with anchor to traces.
- A basic anomaly flag: if cost increases >25% vs baseline and 99p latency doubles, surface as "tenant-econ-exception".

Can you each comment on scope/owners/risks? Marissa — can design mock a small tile showing the summary? Jordan — rough engineering scope (infra/billing changes?) and a quick-high level estimate. Kimberly — what data availability gaps do we have for per-tenant prefix/KV cache hit rates?

ACME is a near-term expansion; they want a demo next quarter as part of the renewal cadence (deal ACME-2029-Q2). I think an MVP that ties together existing tiles + a mini dependency graph would be valuable to more customers than just ACME.

Thanks,
Naomi
Head of Observability Partnerships
Redwood Inference

On Wed, May 15, 2029 at 10:03 Marissa Cole wrote:
> Attaching a quick wireframe...

Thanks — high level response from infra/engineering perspective:

Summary: MVP is feasible but we need to make trade-offs on fidelity vs iteration speed. Proposal below assumes we reuse existing telemetry (token accounting, per-route latency histograms, routing metadata) and add a small batch job to surface cache hit metrics and dependency edges.

MVP components and rough estimate (engineering-level):
- Tile + drill UI (frontend + API): 1.5 sprint (frontend eng + PM support)
- CSV export pipeline (hourly aggregation job + small API): 1 sprint (est. 2 engineer-weeks backend + 1 infra week)
- Dependency matrix: produce an edge list from routing logs + model variants (materialize daily, real-time for spikes requires more work): 2 sprints for a simple graph + traces links
- Cache hit/prefix summary: we currently don't materialize per-tenant prefix-KV metrics. We can approximate via origin logs and a daily aggregator — 2 sprints (needs infra quota for query jobs)
- Alert/anomaly rule: add rule to existing alerting service, plus product toggles: 1 engineer-week

Risks / blockers:
- Billing schema: token-by-model-variant hourly exists but not always tagged with tenant in older accounts — may need a migration or backfill for retrospective exports.
- Storage & cost: hourly aggregation for all tenants increases storage; recommend initial rollout limited to top X tenants (by spend) — an opt-in.
- Ownership: depends on infra (aggregation jobs), billing (schema fix), and observability (traces/dependency edges). We should nominate a single owner to drive cross-team PRs.

Owners I suggest:
- Product: Marissa (PM)
- Frontend: Jordan (owner) + frontend eng (TBD)
- Backend/aggregation: Kim (owner) + infra eng (TBD)
- Billing/backfill: Billing team (contact: rishi_malhotra) — loop them early

If we prioritize for ACME demo, I can scope a "demo mode" that backfills a 30-day view for only their tenant; that reduces storage/work and avoids full schema changes.

Jordan Blake
Staff SW Engineer, Console
Redwood Inference
